name: Voxel Raymarching with DDA and Bounding Box Culling
definition: A rendering technique for sparse, segmented voxel models using a bounding-box mesh as a rasterization footprint. The fragment shader ignores the box geometry, casts a ray from the eye through the pixel, intersects it analytically with the bounding box (ray-AABB slab test), and walks the voxel grid from the entry point with a DDA until it finds a non-empty voxel or leaves the box.
summary: Voxel Raymarching with DDA and Bounding Box Culling is an image-order rendering technique for sparse voxel models that uses DDA traversal and decouples ray origin from box intersection to avoid floating-point errors.
